A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VADD research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison, including identification of removed and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy-distribution, image-generation, and text-generation experiments, including quantitative comparisons, generated samples, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and additionally reports training throughput, new baseline comparisons, and CIFAR-10 samples.

M1.justification: v2 removes VADD-CS, the fixed-latent consistency sampler introduced in v1 Section 3.3 and Algorithm 2. Its sampling algorithm now contains only per-step latent resampling. This removes a substantive inference component; the latent-variable model, recognition architecture, and KL-annealed DELBO objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three toy distributions, binarized MNIST, CIFAR-10, LM1B, OpenWebText, and six zero-shot evaluation corpora. The new comparisons and CIFAR-10 illustrations retain existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 4 replaces the SEDD comparison with EDLM and DCD comparisons alongside MDLM. v2 also compares training speed against EDLM in Table 4 and adds a continuous DDPM baseline for CIFAR-10 in Appendix C.2 and Table 7. SEDD remains in the likelihood tables, so its removal is specific to Figure 4.

E3.justification: Figure 4 changes the comparison axis from sampling steps to sampling time, and new Table 4 evaluates training throughput at batch size 512. Existing data splits, training budgets, sample counts, and likelihood/FID evaluation settings are otherwise retained. The PDFs do not specify a detailed timing measurement protocol.

E4.justification: v2 removes the cross-domain comparison of fixed versus resampled latent variables, including consistency-sampler results and supplementary toy and MNIST illustrations. It adds an empirical training-overhead comparison. The particle-count ablation, fp64 sampling check, and image-training curves remain, despite renumbering and relocation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing 256-sample generative-perplexity averaging and the 1000-particle, 100-pair Monte Carlo likelihood-estimation procedure are unchanged; no new uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Most retained benchmark numbers are unchanged, but the reported evidence changes substantially. v2 adds training speeds of 2.77, 1.74, and 1.84 iterations/s for MDLM, EDLM, and VADD, respectively, plus DDPM FIDs of 298.7 at 10 steps and 77.2 at 100 steps. Figure 4 is replaced by a runtime-based comparison, CIFAR-10 samples are added, and VADD text samples replace VADD-CS examples. Consistency-sampler result series disappear, including its 100-step CIFAR-10 FID of 41.1; retained VADD remains at 50.5.

T1.justification: v2 deletes Appendix A.3, including the consistency-sampler likelihood bounds, cross-entropy assumptions, Propositions 1 and 2, and their proofs in equations (23)–(36). The core DELBO and multi-sample derivations in Appendices A.1–A.2 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion more explicitly restrict superiority claims to sample quality with few denoising steps. The introduction also drops the advertised consistency-sampler contribution. The central claim of improving dimensional-correlation modeling through variational latent variables remains.

C2.justification: New Section 6 identifies the Gaussian prior's prior-hole problem and discusses conditioned or hierarchical priors and alternative training approaches. v2 removes the consistency-sampler mechanism explanation and revises the continuous-image-modeling caveat: its DDPM comparison supports competitiveness in the tested regime while retaining a qualification about stronger continuous methods.

D1.justification: v2 adds an official code-release statement and link, and identifies the DDPM pipeline and pretrained checkpoint used for the new comparison. Conversely, Appendix B removes the A100/H800 hardware specifications for the experiments. These documentation changes do not establish that the underlying hardware or retained training settings changed.

R1.justification: Section 4 substantially expands positioning against distillation methods, adding Di[M]O, Soft-Di[M]O, and Learnable Sampler Distillation and emphasizing training without a pretrained teacher. It also adds a substantive discussion of posterior-collapse remedies and associated references; the limitations section adds prior-learning references.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact. v2 folds sampling into Section 3.2, renumbers the architecture subsection, adds a limitations section, expands related work, and makes focused introductory and concluding edits. It also updates affiliations and front matter and removes a duplicated preprocessing paragraph from Appendix B.3.

P2.justification: The visual presentation changes extensively: Figure 1 becomes a horizontal arrangement, Figure 3 redisplays VADD samples previously in the appendix, and Figure 4 receives a new axis and comparator legend. New throughput and DDPM tables and a CIFAR-10 sample grid are added; consistency-sampler displays are removed. The conference template and relocation of appendix tables further reorganize the layout.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves support and calibration for the retained VADD contribution through additional baseline comparisons, empirical training-cost measurements, narrower few-step claims, and an explicit prior-hole limitation. The code-release statement also improves access information. These gains are tempered by removal of the consistency-sampler analysis and hardware specifications, particularly because the new timing comparisons remain insufficiently documented.
